title: Strict localizations above the closed point of a strict-local base change
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], put $S'=S_{(\bar s)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and let $\bar s':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S'$ be its canonical closed-point lift [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](1). Set $X'=X\times_SS'$ with projections $p:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\bar x':\operatorname{Spec}\Xi\to X'$ be a geometric point and let $a:\operatorname{Spec}\Xi\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ satisfy $f'\bar x'=\bar s'a$. Write $\bar x=p\bar x'$ and $\bar u=f\bar x$, and form the functorial maps of strict localizations [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](3)-(4). Then the canonical maps
$$S'_{(f'\bar x')}\longrightarrow S',\qquad S'\longrightarrow S_{(\bar u)},\qquad X'_{(\bar x')}\longrightarrow X_{(\bar x)}$$
are isomorphisms. Here the middle map is the functorial map $S'_{(f'\bar x')}\to S_{(\bar u)}$ composed with the inverse of the first map. The last isomorphism commutes with the maps to $X$ and, using $S'\cong S_{(\bar u)}$, with the maps to $S'$. In particular, for every geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'\to S'$, it induces an isomorphism over $X$
$$X'_{(\bar x')}\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'\ \cong\ X_{(\bar x)}\times_{S_{(\bar u)}}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega',$$
where the map on the right is $\bar t$ followed by $S'\to S_{(\bar u)}$. No finiteness or properness of $f$, or algebraicity of $\Xi/\Omega$ or $\Omega'$ over its image residue field, is assumed.

proof.text: For any geometric point y, use the existing local-structure theorem for its chosen strict-local ring H_y. The canonical evaluation H_y -> Omega is the composite of its codomain restriction to the relative separable closure and the inclusion into Omega. The restriction is surjective, hence local, and the field inclusion is local. Thus evaluation is local and its spectrum sends the field point to the closed point of H_y. Composing the closed-point lift equation with the unique point of Spec Omega shows that the structural map j_y sends the closed point to the image of y.

Every j_y is weakly etale. Choose an affine open Spec R -> Y containing the image of y. Every point of Spec H_y generalizes its closed point, so j_y factors through that open. Write the factor as Spec alpha using full faithfulness of Spec. The affine-chart lemma makes alpha ind-etale, hence weakly etale. An open immersion is etale and therefore weakly etale; composition proves the assertion for j_y.

Base change of j_s in the given cartesian square makes p weakly etale. The equations q followed by j_x equals j_xprime followed by p, and b followed by j_u equals j_uprime followed by j_s, make these two composites weakly etale. Cancel the weakly etale maps j_x and j_u using Mathlib WeaklyEtale.of_comp. Its elementary diagonal argument is as follows: for maps r followed by g with both g and the composite weakly etale, the diagonal of g is weakly etale because it is flat and its own diagonal is an isomorphism (a diagonal is mono). The graph of r is its base change and therefore weakly etale. The projection after the graph is the base change of the weakly etale composite. Their composition is r, which is thus weakly etale. No affine base-change comparison is needed.

proof.text: Evaluate the pointed equations for b and q at the unique point of Spec Xi. Step 1 identifies their evaluation images with the respective closed points, so b and q carry closed point to closed point; their corresponding ring homomorphisms are local. The target strict-local rings are strictly henselian. Olivier’s theorem for a local weakly etale ring map out of a strictly henselian ring therefore makes b and q isomorphisms. Also hclosed places xprime followed by fprime at the closed point of H_s: the map a sends the unique point of Spec Xi to the unique point of Spec Omega. Thus j_uprime is local on rings, and the same theorem makes it an isomorphism. Define e as the inverse of j_uprime followed by b. The equation j_uprime followed by e equals b and the equation e followed by j_u equals j_s follow by cancelling the inverse.

proof.text: Compare q followed by d and j_xprime followed by fprime followed by e. Their composites with j_u agree by hd, hq, the cartesian square and the base equation for e. Their composites with the distinguished evaluation of xprime agree by hqpoint, hdpoint, hbpoint, j_uprime followed by e equals b, and the closed-point lift equations. For each affine pointed etale neighbourhood of u, compose the two maps with its strict-local limit leg and its affine-scheme identification. Both maps have the same base and pointed composites. Etale pointed-map rigidity, applied to the local evaluation from H_xprime into Xi, identifies them. The strict-local limit universal property then identifies the original maps, giving the required compatibility with the new base.

For any geometric point t of the new base, form pullback.map using q on the first factors, the identity on Spec Omega-prime, and e on the bases. The preceding compatibility is its first commutative square, and the second is the identity equation. All three maps are isomorphisms; their inverses induce the inverse pullback map, as checked on the two projections. The standard pullback.map projection equations are exactly the two asserted equations. Together with hq, the first projection equation also gives compatibility over X. Nothing in the construction assumes an algebraic field extension.
